sources.entry: Swiftcord - Native Discord client built in Swift & SwiftUI. Light on your RAM and CPU.

summary.one_liner: Swiftcord is a native SwiftUI Discord client for macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 26+) with Liquid Glass styling.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Swiftcord as a 100% native SwiftUI Discord client for macOS. It states that it uses system controls so that it fits in with the Mac, and that messages, rich text, and embeds are meant to render as expected. The project says it was rebuilt with performance as a focus, with claims of fast launch, quick switching between conversations, and low resource use. It is currently available for macOS 26+ on Apple Silicon, and the README says iOS support is coming soon. The README also points to X and Discord channels for updates and community chat, and notes that the legacy codebase is archived on the main branch.
use_cases: Chatting on Discord from a Mac
Using Discord as a native macOS app instead of a browser tab
Running a lightweight Discord client on Apple Silicon
Studying a SwiftUI app built for macOS
notable: Native SwiftUI build using system controls, with Liquid Glass styling
Rebuilt from the ground up with performance as a stated goal
Rich text and embeds rendering in Discord messages
Legacy codebase preserved on the main branch
caveats: Requires macOS 26 or later on Apple Silicon
iOS support is listed as coming soon, not yet available
The README gives no install or build instructions
